archetype.name: Improviser (dual-threat)
archetype.definition: A third-year QB whose production leans on holding the ball, breaking the pocket and turning scrambles into first downs, more than on-schedule timing throws.

report.headline: Two-game sample shows real growth, but the hamstring stalls it and threatens his legs
report.take:
Caleb Williams is a creator first. He holds the ball 3.42 seconds, was pressured on 40% of dropbacks (the most of any qualifier), and still finished the drives that mattered by scrambling on 14.3% of dropbacks for 0.914 EPA per scramble and six first downs on ten tries. That is the engine. The structured run game around him did nothing: designed runs were stuffed on 3 of 5. His rushing value comes from broken plays, not called ones.

The passing numbers look like a step forward: +5.5 CPOE (12th), 0.292 EPA per dropback (7th), and a bad-throw rate of 10.9% after two years near the bottom of the league at 18.5% and 17.8%. He also kept the 2025 gain in sack avoidance. His pressure-to-sack rate was 43.5% as a rookie (60th of 63), 15.9% last year and 20.8% now, so turning pressure into escapes rather than sacks is a skill that has held for two seasons. The accuracy jump is the part to doubt. He ran a negative CPOE in both prior seasons, and 55 attempts can't overturn 34 games.

The two games also point in opposite directions. Week 1 was a 59-37 shootout in Carolina: 269 yards, a +16.6 CPOE and 37.3 PPR points. Week 2 against Minnesota, now the top-ranked defense, was a 3-9 loss. He threw 138 yards with -1.0 pass EPA, and his intended air yards fell to 3.9 as 21 blitzes pushed him into checkdowns. The season line is mostly the Carolina game. Within one score he was a modest 0.134 EPA per play with 40% success.

Now the hamstring takes over. He is Out, held out of Week 5 practice, called week-to-week, with an estimated return of October 18. Case Keenum has started the last two games. The worry isn't only lost time. A strained hamstring hits the scrambling that makes his profile work. When he returns, starting tackle Braxton Jones (65% of snaps) will be on IR until November, and he is already the most-pressured QB in the sample.

strengths.title: Scrambles that bail out drives
strengths.body: His 10 scrambles produced 86 yards, six first downs and 0.914 EPA each, far more than his designed runs produced. This is a long-standing trait: he ranked 7th among QBs in rushing yards in both 2024 and 2025. It lasts as long as the hamstring lets him move freely.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer becomes sacks
strengths.body: A 20.8% pressure-to-sack rate (9th) on the heaviest pressure load in the league shows he escapes rather than goes down. The 2025 jump from 60th to 5th in this stat makes it look like real development, not luck.

strengths.title: Cleaner ball placement
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate fell to 10.9% (14th) after he sat 55th and 52nd the past two seasons. Together with a +5.5 CPOE, it is the most encouraging passing sign. It is also the most fragile, coming on 55 attempts with one big game carrying it.

concerns.title: Hamstring hits his core skill
concerns.body: He is Out and week-to-week, with an estimated return of October 18 and Keenum starting in his place. A strained hamstring is the injury most likely to dull the scramble value his profile depends on, even after he is cleared.

concerns.title: Most-pressured QB, thinner line ahead
concerns.body: He was pressured on 40% of dropbacks, 32nd of 32. Some of that is the cost of holding the ball to create, but losing left tackle Braxton Jones to IR until November makes it harder. The team's 4th-ranked hit rate allowed suggests the line is fine when the ball comes out on time, which points back to his own style.

concerns.title: Blitzes shrank his throws
concerns.body: Minnesota blitzed him 21 times, and his intended air yards collapsed to 3.9 in a 138-yard game. He has been blitzed on 55% of dropbacks and throws 2.74 yards short of the sticks on average. Good defenses have a blueprint, and it holds until he punishes the extra rusher.

trend.note: He opened with a 37-point fantasy shootout, followed it with a 3-point offensive dud against the league's best defense, and then got hurt. Two games and two extremes don't make a trajectory.

nextGame.headline: Soft Packers defense, but Williams is unlikely to suit up
nextGame.body:
If he were playing, Green Bay would suit him. The Packers rank 27th in defensive EPA and 25th against the pass, Micah Parsons is out, and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is done for the year with a torn Achilles. The catch is that Green Bay allows explosive pass plays only 4.7% of the time (4th), so it makes you earn yards in chunks. That favors an offense that can stay on schedule over one built on second-reaction plays.

Availability decides this game. Williams is Out, didn't practice, is week-to-week, and has an estimated return a week after this game, so plan on Case Keenum, who started Weeks 3 and 4. On the other side, Green Bay's line is battered: center Jacob Monk (96% of snaps) and guard Aaron Banks are out, and tackle Zach Bako-Bewele is on IR. They face a Bears defense with the 4th-best sack rate and 2nd-best pass defense. Kyle Monangai's thumb (questionable) is the Bears' only other offensive question.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush vs depleted GB line
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay already allows the second-highest hit rate in the league. It is now without its starting center and a guard, and has lost a tackle to IR. Chicago's defense ranks 4th in sack rate and 2nd in pass EPA, so this is the clearest edge in the game.

keyMatchups.title: GB's run game can't punish CHI
keyMatchups.body: Chicago's soft spot is run defense (28th), but Green Bay has the league's worst rushing offense by EPA. That weakness probably stays hidden this week.

keyMatchups.title: Bears passing vs leaky but tight GB
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay gives up efficiency through the air (25th in pass EPA) but few big plays (4th in explosive rate). That shapes up as long drives for whoever is at quarterback for Chicago.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams is downgraded off the week-to-week tag, and how freely he moves in his first practice back. Scramble readiness matters more than whether he is active.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect him back around the October 18 estimate, though week-to-week hamstrings often run long, and expect the first game or two back to be pocket-heavy. The sack avoidance and willingness to hold the ball look like who he is now. The +5.5 CPOE and 0.292 EPA per dropback are inflated by the Carolina shootout, and his history says the accuracy settles near league average rather than staying near the top. The best guide is his 2025 baseline: about 232 passing yards and 23 rushing yards a game. That should hold inside a run-leaning Ben Johnson offense that passes 3.9% less than expected.

The rushing TD pace (two in two games) will come down, and so will the fantasy line built on it. He should still be a useful dual-threat starter. The ceiling depends on the hamstring and on how Chicago protects him without Jones.
swingFactors: Pass protection until Braxton Jones returns
Whether the CPOE gain survives a larger sample

bets.reason: Even with Keenum, Chicago's offense ranks 8th in EPA and its defense 5th, against a Green Bay offense ranked 25th. The Packers are also missing their center, a guard and a tackle against the Bears' 4th-ranked sack rate. The Bears also lose a lot by having Williams out and had a 3-9 dud against Minnesota, so this is a lean, not a like.

Green Bay's offense is 25th by EPA and last on the ground, and its defense allows few explosive passes (4th). Chicago passes less than expected (23rd in pass rate over expected), which points to long, clock-eating drives in a division game.

confidence.note: Two games and 55 attempts, he is out with a week-to-week hamstring, and a backup QB is starting the next game.
